statements.text: Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets in the Solar System.
statements.note: Venus has retrograde rotation, so it spins clockwise when viewed from above the Sun's north pole.

statements.text: Mars is the hottest planet in the Solar System.
statements.note: Venus is the hottest. Its thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface around 465 °C.

statements.text: One rotation of Venus takes longer than one Venusian year.
statements.note: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

explanation: Mars is cold. Venus is the Solar System's hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

statements.text: Octopuses have three hearts.
statements.note: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and a third pumps it around the body.

statements.text: All bat species are completely blind.
statements.note: No bat is blind. Many bats use echolocation, but they can all see, and fruit bats rely heavily on their eyesight.

statements.text: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
statements.note: Their unusual wing movement lets them hover and even fly backwards.

explanation: “Blind as a bat” is a myth. All bats can see.

statements.text: An adult human skeleton typically has 206 bones.
statements.note: Babies are born with more bones, and many of them fuse as the body grows.

statements.text: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the human body.
statements.note: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

statements.text: The smallest bone in the human body is in the foot.
statements.note: The smallest bone is the stapes, found in the middle ear.

explanation: The smallest bone is the stapes in the ear, not a bone in the foot.

statements.text: Russia spans 11 time zones.
statements.note: Russia has used 11 time zones since 2014, from Kaliningrad in the west to Kamchatka in the east.

statements.text: The Nile and the Amazon are the two longest rivers in the world.
statements.note: Which of the two is longer depends on how they are measured, but these two rivers are the top two.

source.title: List of river systems by length

statements.text: Counting polar deserts, the Sahara is the largest desert on Earth.
statements.note: A desert is defined by low rainfall, not heat. Antarctica is the largest desert, and the Sahara is the largest hot desert.

explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert because deserts are defined by rainfall, not temperature.

statements.text: Water expands when it freezes.
statements.note: Ice is less dense than liquid water, which is why it floats.

statements.text: Sunlight takes roughly eight minutes to reach Earth.
statements.note: At the average Earth–Sun distance, light takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

statements.text: Sound travels faster through air than through water.
statements.note: Sound travels about four times faster in water (around 1,480 m/s) than in air (around 343 m/s).

explanation: Sound moves much faster through water than through air.

statements.text: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889.
statements.note: It was built as the entrance to the 1889 World's Fair in Paris.

statements.text: The Great Wall of China is easily visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
statements.note: It's a myth. The wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon, and it is hard to spot even from low Earth orbit.

statements.text: The first crewed Moon landing took place in 1969.
statements.note: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.

explanation: You cannot see the Great Wall from the Moon with the naked eye.

statements.text: Bananas are classified as berries in botany.
statements.note: Botanically, a banana is a berry: a fleshy fruit that develops from a single ovary.

statements.text: Strawberries are not true berries in botany.
statements.note: A strawberry is an “accessory fruit”, and its “seeds” are actually tiny individual fruits.

statements.text: Peanuts are tree nuts that grow on branches.
statements.note: Peanuts are legumes, and their pods develop underground.

explanation: Peanuts are legumes that grow underground. They are not tree nuts.

statements.text: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
statements.note: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined.

statements.text: Saturn's average density is lower than the density of water.
statements.note: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³, while water's is 1 g/cm³.

statements.text: Pluto is officially classified as the ninth planet.
statements.note: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.

explanation: Pluto has been classified as a dwarf planet since 2006.

statements.text: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.
statements.note: Blue whales can be around 30 m long, bigger than any known dinosaur.

statements.text: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
statements.note: It's a myth. Experiments show goldfish can remember things for months.

statements.text: Eucalyptus leaves make up most of a koala's diet.
statements.note: Koalas live in eucalyptus woodland and eat mostly eucalyptus leaves, a low-energy diet that keeps them asleep around 20 hours a day.

explanation: Goldfish can remember things for months, not just seconds.

statements.text: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.
statements.note: Mandarin has roughly 900 million or more native speakers.

source.title: List of languages by number of native speakers

statements.text: The Olympic Games originated in ancient Greece.
statements.note: The ancient Games were held at Olympia, traditionally starting in 776 BC.

statements.text: Vatican City is larger in area than Monaco.
statements.note: Vatican City covers about 0.49 km² and Monaco about 2 km². The Vatican is the smallest country in the world.

explanation: Vatican City is the world's smallest country, about a quarter of the size of Monaco.

statements.text: Diamonds are made of carbon.
statements.note: Diamond is a form of pure carbon, with its atoms arranged in a crystal lattice.

statements.text: Gold is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust.
statements.note: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the crust. Gold is extremely rare.

source.title: Abundance of elements in Earth's crust

statements.text: Helium is lighter than air.
statements.note: Helium is much less dense than air, which is why helium balloons float.

explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust. Gold is one of the rarest.
